To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the low-complexity C-terminal tail of M. smegmatis KU modulates DNA binding; (ii) the lysine-rich PAKKA repeats in the tail of KU contribute to DNA end-joining; and (iii) the PAKKA sequences are also present in the Hlp histone-like protein, where they have been shown previously to contribute to end apposition.
the low-complexity C-terminal extension of M. smegmatis KU modulates DNA binding and promotes end-joining.
the C-terminal extension of M. smegmatis DNA-PK (Ku protein), containing low-complexity repeats, modulates DNA end-joining.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the C-terminal extension of Mycobacteriaceae Ku and how its low-complexity sequences contribute to DNA binding and end-joining.
the role of the lysine rich low-complexity repeats in DNA binding and end-joining activity of Ku protein.
the structure and function of Ku, a protein involved in the DNA repair pathway of non-homologous DNA end joining.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the C-terminal lysine-rich tail is not required for DNA binding but is involved in modulating the affinity of Ku for DNA ends.
the PAKKAs of Ku are a novel and important component of the DNA end-joining machinery of Mycobacterrium smegmatis.
the lysine-rich C-terminal extension of Mycobacterial Ku modulates DNA end binding and promotes end joining by T4 DNA Ligase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the C-terminal extension of M. smegmatis Kus modulates the DNA-binding affinity of Ku and promotes DNA end- joining by T4 DNA Ligase.
the lysine-rich C-terminal tail of M. smegmatis KU enhances DNA end-joining, but it does not contribute to DNA binding.
Ku protein from mycobacteria has evolved a C-terminal extension that is not required for DNA binding, but which enhances the efficiency of end-joining by an exogenous ligase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lysine-rich PAKKA repeats of M. smegmatis are dispensable for DNA binding but are required for optimal NHEJ.
low-complexly lysine-rich repeats can function as an intrinsic DNA binding domain.
low-complexy sequences have evolved repeatedly for modulating the function of DNA-binding proteins.
